text:
sasha: Heads up — seeing a weird pattern in kvcache during today's long-context load test. Residency% for pool-gpu-2 dropped ~30% around 12:07 UTC, eviction_count spiked, and yet resident_bytes kept growing for ~10m after. attaching quick profiler excerpt below. anyone else see this?
perf-bot: ALERT: kvcache_eviction_rate{pool="pool-gpu-2"} > 5000/min (12:07 UTC). See: https://perf.redwood/alerts/EVT-842 :rotating_light:
lee: can you paste the PromQL you used? prepping a dashboard patch now.
sasha: here's the rough PromQL I grabbed from the ad-hoc query: `sum by(pool) (increase(kvcache_eviction_count_total[1m]))` and `kvcache_resident_bytes{pool="pool-gpu-2"}`. profiler snippet:```
[kv-profiler] pool=pool-gpu-2 ts=2026-03-18T12:07:22Z
  frag_allocations: 12834
  frag_reuse_count: 1542
  frag_reuse_rate: 0.12
  avg_fragment_size_bytes: 409
  eviction_ops: 5234
  avg_eviction_age_seconds: 26.4
  resident_bytes: 78.3GB
```
maria: interesting — frag_reuse_rate that low + small avg fragment size explains fragmentation growth. we saw a similar pattern in feb where small writes after a batching change caused lots of tiny KV buffers and inefficient compaction.
jamal: FYI I rolled out the new batching heuristic to pool-gpu-2 yesterday morning (canary). it batches aggressively per-request which can create more frequent small-key writes into the KV cache. might explain the spike.
sasha: ok makes sense. two asks: (1) add an `eviction_age_seconds` histogram (buckets e.g. [1,5,15,30,60,300]) and `kvcache_fragmentation_ratio = 1 - (compacted_bytes / raw_bytes)` as a gauge; (2) dashboard: show eviction rate, median eviction_age, frag_reuse_rate, resident_bytes, and per-model residency_percent heatmap for top 10 models. also propose an alert: `increase(kvcache_eviction_count_total[5m]) > 2000` for pool-level.
lee: I'll open a dashboard PR and wire the new histogram panels + heatmap. PromQL for median eviction age: `histogram_quantile(0.5, sum(rate(eviction_age_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,pool))`. adding the suggested alert rule.
maria: for fragmentation_ratio we should instrument `compacted_bytes_total` and `raw_bytes_total` in runtime before deriving the gauge. also recommend sampling residency per-request to avoid high-cardinality metrics — store top-k models per-pool.
jamal: I'll rollback the canary on pool-gpu-2 to previous batching config for the next 30m while we validate. on it.
sasha: thanks — can we also enable a short-lived trace (1s sampling) for requests that triggered eviction spikes so we can capture exact callsites? would help confirm whether the small writes are from our batching paths or something else.
lee: yeah, I'll add a temporary trace tag and update the runbook with the new metric names and alert thresholds.
maria: notes for impl: histogram buckets: [0.1,0.5,1,2,5,10,30,60,120,300], frag_reuse_rate as `kvcache_frag_reuse_total / kvcache_frag_alloc_total`. will add comments in PR.
sasha: perfect. if anyone sees more spikes after rollback call out in this thread. :thumbsup:
jamal: reverted canary at 12:13 UTC, monitoring.
perf-bot: NOTE: alert resolved for pool-gpu-2 at 12:14 UTC (EVT-842).
sasha: ack. thanks all — follow-ups: dashboard PR (lee), fragmentation instrumentation PR (maria), rollback validation (jamal).
lee: on it, will tag you both in the PR.
maria: prepping code + unit tests, ETA 3 hours.
jamal: monitoring looks quieter so far.
sasha: closing the loop later today with a quick postmortem snippet.
lee: cool. :rocket:
